note_on_kvness: This is a KNOWN task, but I include it in the Lane A rotation because the task_memory shows opus-everywhere SILVER and sonnet-everywhere INVALID (E045/E046). Question: does the agentic per-node router solve this without needing opus-everywhere?

router_decisions: Per-node router escalated opus-coder + opus-designer + opus-reviser on node 6 (designer=opus-4-8, coder=opus-4-8, reviser=opus-4-8) — heaviest escalation seen in the campaign so far. outcome.fail_reason: Engine declared 'Budget exhausted, stopping' at +1h51m. Drained 1 straggler for ~6min then SIGKILL by wrapper at +1h57m. No aggregator run → no submission.csv.

failed_nodes.node_2: training crashed — HF transformers AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained failed (likely tokenizer/model name issue in agent code)

interpretation:
The router did exactly what task_memory implied: ratchet up to opus-everywhere on coder/designer/reviser, predicting spooky-author needs higher capability. But the per-node-routing latency + opus latency + 6-node search depth exceeded the 2h pipeline budget BEFORE aggregator could run.

This is a budget/latency problem, not a router quality problem. The signal that the router 'knows' spooky-author is hard is itself valuable — but at the current 6-node, 10-min-per-node, opus-on-3-roles configuration, the wall-clock budget runs out.
key_observations: spooky-author CONFIRMS router uses task-knowledge: it predicted opus-needed and routed accordingly.
But this revealed a NEW failure mode: budget-cap-before-aggregator. 4 nodes succeeded with good models but no merge.
Workaround for future spooky-author runs: either (a) reduce designs+nodes to fit budget, (b) raise budget to 3-4h, or (c) accept Lane A scout incomplete and move to Lane B target run.
actions_for_future_runs: Consider --budget 20 --nodes 4 for known-hard text tasks like spooky-author and jigsaw.
Skip retry under same settings — would just repeat the wall-clock cap.
